content.comment_body: Hello, experts, We have a small SCADA system where the server usually communicates with remote stations using MODBUS protocol over GPRS. We need to add more remote stations and are considering using [company_name] [product_name] modules. Is it possible to achieve this with [product_name] CMR and BM modules? Our plan is to connect to the [product_name] BM remotely via VPN (over GPRS) and obtain variable states through Modbus TCP. Thank you in advance. [user_name]

With [version_no], you can set up your application via VPN. On the CMR module, you can configure up to 4 ports to be forwarded to the [product_name] BM through VPN. The [product_name] BM should be set to use the CMR as the default gateway. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, experts, Is there a way to do this without using a VPN? Perhaps there's a router from [company_name] supporting Virtual Server capabilities, allowing direct access to [product_name] with Modbus via a static IP?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are evaluating technical options for MODBUS TCP/IP communication via GPRS between a SCADA system and [company_name] [product_name] modules, referring to CMR and BM hardware. Key concerns include whether a VPN is required or if direct access over static IP is possible, suggesting that current documentation may lack clarity on these network configurations. There's interest in flexible and simple connectivity solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [company_name] [product_name] modules to support reliable MODBUS TCP/IP communication over GPRS, achievable through either VPN or direct access with static IP. Clear and user-friendly networking setups are desired to simplify integration.
pain_keywords: lack of direct access via static IP
